githook-no-hookspath._why: THE FAST PATH, which is most repositories. No core.hooksPath at all, so the literal is absent from the config text and the heal returns before it runs a single git subprocess. This case exists because the git half rides the SessionStart hook that fires in every project on the machine: a cost paid here is paid on every session start everywhere.

githook-settled._why: githook-stranded AFTER THE HEAL, run again: no hooksPath, no guard directory, the carried-across post-merge in the repository's own hooks directory, and a sidecar with no git_config. The second run must do and say nothing. `bin/idempotence` asserts the same property by running the writer twice against one tree; this asserts it against the settled state as a tree of its own, so a regression that re-created the directory or re-wrote the sidecar is visible as a case rather than as a diff.

githook-prior-tracked._why: A TRACKED RECORD MUST NOT CHOOSE WHERE GIT LOOKS FOR EXECUTABLE HOOKS. `.settings-owned.json` is tracked in nsayka-wawa and odyssey-alive (measured 2026-10-10), so on a clone its `prior` is whatever the tree's author wrote, and the heal hands that value to `git config --local core.hooksPath`. A tracked `prior` pointing at a tracked directory with a tracked `pre-commit` in it would be a committed file arranging for its own script to run on the next commit. Provenance is the only test that separates this from the legitimate case, because every shape test passes: the record here is identical to githook-prior-restored's and the only difference is that this one is committed. The recorded value is REPORTED and not applied, and core.hooksPath is unset instead -- so the guard still goes and the hook that lived only in the guard directory still lands in the directory git will actually read.

githook-link-in-guard._why: A SYMLINK IN THE GUARD DIRECTORY IS NEVER COPIED. Copying it would read the link's target and write those bytes into the directory git runs hooks out of, with the source file's mode -- so a tracked link named `post-merge` pointing at any tracked file in the repository installs that file as an executable git hook (CWE-59, flagged on 73c5908). The link is left exactly where it is, reported, and the directory therefore stays. `.git/hooks/post-merge` staying ABSENT is the whole assertion: nothing was carried across.

githook-dangling-target._why: A DANGLING SYMLINK AT THE TARGET NAME. `os.path.exists` answers False for a link whose target is absent, so a missing-file test reads the name as free and `shutil.copy2` then FOLLOWS the link and writes an executable wherever it points -- outside the hooks directory, outside the project if the link says so (CWE-59, flagged on 73c5908). `lexists` is the test, a link at that name is refused and reported, and the guard copy stays. The link is made at run time because a dangling one cannot be checked in: bin/check requires every tracked fixture link to resolve to something git carries.

want: lives ONLY in the guard directory

githook-prior-unknown._why: THE PROVENANCE CHECK MUST FAIL CLOSED. `_tracked` answers by running `git ls-files`, and a nonzero exit means the question could not be ASKED -- a corrupt or unreadable index, no git on PATH, a timeout -- which is not the same as `no, nothing is tracked`. Reading it as untracked applies a hooks path out of a file whose provenance was never established, which is the whole of the rule githook-prior-tracked pins (review of 862da37; before the fix this tree set core.hooksPath to scripts/hooks). The tree is githook-prior-restored byte for byte, with one broken index on top, so the opposite decision is isolated to that one difference. The report line says the same thing about the deletion rather than asserting `unstaged` about files nothing could classify.
want: git could not say whether it is tracked

githook-prior-restored._why: A RECORDED NON-NULL PRIOR, IN AN UNTRACKED RECORD. `--install-hook` recorded the EXACT value core.hooksPath held before it took it, and the heal restores that rather than unsetting: a repository that ran its hooks out of scripts/hooks before the guard arrived must run them out of scripts/hooks afterwards. It also moves the target the guard copies are compared against, which is why the hooks directory is resolved and never a literal .git/hooks. NOTHING IS COMMITTED HERE, and that is now load-bearing rather than incidental: an untracked `.settings-owned.json` is a local-only record, written by the install that actually ran in this working tree, and only such a record is allowed to choose a hooks path (githook-prior-tracked is the same tree committed, and does not restore). githook-divergent-copy._why: A COPY THAT DIVERGED IS NEVER DELETED. The guard's post-merge and the repository's own post-merge are different files here, so there is no way to tell which one the user wants: both are left in place, the difference is reported, and the directory therefore stays. Measured 2026-10-10 in nsayka-wawa, all four git-lfs hooks were byte-identical to the ones in .git/hooks, which is the only reason the whole directory can ever go -- a deletion rule that assumed that would destroy an edited hook.

githook-foreign-precommit._why: A pre-commit THAT IS NOT THE GUARD. The deletion rule is the wf-pin-check header and nothing else, so somebody's own script sitting at that name is carried across to the resolved hooks directory instead of being deleted -- unsetting core.hooksPath on top of it would stop running it with no message anywhere. The plan's own risk list names this: unsetting turns off any hook that existed only in the guard directory.

code-origin-not-git._why: The hook runs before every edit in every project, git or not. Outside a repository there is no history to classify, so it must stay silent and exit 0 rather than guess authorship from style.

artifact-style-quickstart._why: The quickstart is the Artifact tool's mandated first call for any new artifact, so it is the one point where the house style can arrive BEFORE a line of the page exists. It must name the skill and carry the HTML-vs-Docs routing rule, and it must never deny: nothing has been written yet.

artifact-style-docs-create._why: The Artifact tool's other door into Claude Docs: `publish` with a type_url and no local file. This is how the efwnow orientation brief the user called 'hard on the eyes' was born (2026-10-02). User directive 2026-10-15: 'workforce should always enforce this format for shareable documentation'. With no transcript there are no user words naming Docs, so it is refused, and the refusal names the HTML route.

artifact-style-docs-birth-brief._why: THE REPORTED CASE (odyssey-alive 0a159bc6, 2026-10-15). The Docs server says the doc skeleton is the turn's first tool call, so the Artifact quickstart never ran and an orientation brief was born in the Docs viewer. The user asked for 'an online shareable doc', which is shareable documentation, not co-editing. The refusal must say it overrides the server's first-call instruction and name the HTML route, or the model holds two orders and picks the louder one.
want: OVERRIDES the Claude Docs server's instruction
if your Artifact tool offers it
Instead, load the `shared-artifact` skill first; it is the required step.

artifact-style-docs-retry-denied._why: A RETRY IS REFUSED LIKE THE FIRST ATTEMPT. The user's directive (2026-10-15, 'I shouldn't have to ask') takes the choice away from the model, so nothing the model writes opens the gate: not its own text claiming co-editing is the point, not the shared-artifact skill body (a meta row) that names Claude Docs and co-editing, not a tool result echoing the refusal, and not a task notification saying the user wants Docs. Only the user's words count, and these ask for 'an online document I can share'.
want: Do not retry the Docs call

artifact-style-docs-user-asked._why: THE ONE WAY THROUGH. The user's own words, in a later message of the session, ask for a Claude Doc they can edit together and comment in. That is the case Docs exists for, and refusing it would be a wrong fire on an explicit request.

artifact-style-docs-other-prefix._why: The birth is matched by tool-name pattern, not by this machine's `mcp__claude_ai_Claude_Docs__` prefix, so a host that names the connector differently is covered. No transcript_path at all: a session whose user words cannot be read opens nothing, so the birth is refused.

artifact-style-docs-update-silent._why: An edit to a doc that already exists: `batch` with a container id and no `create`. Every write after a birth goes this way (34 updates and 4 batch edits in the two Docs sessions on the measuring machine), and refusing them would strand a doc the user asked for.

artifact-style-docs-read-silent._why: A read writes nothing. The registered matcher never routes `read` here, and the hook's own name check stays silent too when a broader registration does.

artifact-style-docs-comment-silent._why: `create` is also how a comment is made: object `utterance` into an existing container, with no `container.create`. MEASURED: the one `create` call on the measuring machine is exactly this. A comment on a doc is not a doc birth.

artifact-style-open-silent._why: `open` shows an existing artifact in the viewer and writes nothing. The reported session's only Artifact call was this, on the doc the Docs birth had just made.

artifact-style-docs-queued-ask._why: REVIEW FINDING 1. A message the user types while the model is busy is stored only as an `attachment` row of type `queued_command`, never as a user row. 115 of them on the measuring machine carry origin kind `human`. Here the user's ask for a Claude Doc to edit together arrived that way, and ignoring it would refuse an explicit request.

artifact-style-docs-queued-not-user._why: THE OTHER HALF OF FINDING 1. Task notifications and peer-session messages also arrive as `queued_command` attachments: commandMode `task-notification`, origin kind `peer` with isMeta, or text `INJECTED` recognises. None is the user, so each names Claude Docs and co-editing here and the birth is still refused.

artifact-style-docs-skill-asked._why: REVIEW FINDING 2. Typing a Docs skill (`/docs`, `/anthropic-skills:docs`) is asking for Docs by name, but the skill's name is in `<command-name>` and its args need not say 'Claude Docs'. Refusing it would block the user's own command.

artifact-style-docs-negated-denied._why: REVIEW FINDING 5, NARROWED BY THE SECOND REVIEW. 'Don’t use Claude Docs' and 'do not put it in Claude Docs' name Docs to refuse it. Decided by verb scope in the mention's clause: both carry a verb after the negation, and the verb is itself negated. The curly apostrophe is how this user types.

artifact-style-docs-plain-ask._why: REVIEW FINDING 6. A plain ask for Docs need not say 'Claude Docs' or 'co-edit': 'set it up in Docs so the whole team can collaborate on the rota' is the case Docs exists for. Since the second review, 'in Docs' needs the capital D and 'collaborate on' needs a document noun after it.

artifact-style-docs-instead-of-asked._why: SECOND REVIEW FINDING 1. 'Instead of HTML use Claude Docs' asks for Docs. Treating 'instead of' as a negation refused it, because the window reached back over 'HTML use'.

artifact-style-docs-why-not-asked._why: SECOND REVIEW FINDING 1. 'Why not use Claude Docs' is a suggestion to use it. 'not use' is a negation on the verb, so `why` directly before it has to cancel the negation.

artifact-style-docs-no-put-asked._why: SECOND REVIEW FINDING 1. 'No put it in Claude docs' answers a question with no, then asks for Docs. A bare 'no' in the window refused it. Under the verb-scope rule the verb 'put' follows the 'no' and is not itself negated.

artifact-style-docs-repo-talk-denied._why: SECOND REVIEW FINDING 3. Talk about a repository's docs is not an ask for Claude Docs. None of these opens the gate: 'update the readme in docs' (lowercase, a directory), 'we should collaborate on this' (no document noun), 'check both edited files', and 'the changelog file was co-edited'. The user's actual ask is a release summary to share, so the birth is refused.

artifact-style-docs-refusals-denied._why: THIRD REVIEW. Each of these refuses Docs, and the second review's verb-only negation let all five through: 'Not Claude Docs, HTML', 'No Claude Docs please', 'never Claude Docs', 'not in Claude Docs', and 'Don’t put the orientation brief in Claude Docs', where the noun phrase pushed the negation out of a four-word window. Under the verb-scope rule, a mention with no verb between it and the last negation word in its clause is negated. When a verb is there, the mention is negated only if that verb is.

artifact-style-docs-not-just-asked._why: THIRD REVIEW, THE ALLOW SIDE. 'not just a page put it in Claude Docs': the verb 'put' sits between the negation and the mention and is not itself negated, so this is an ask.

artifact-style-docs-without-asked._why: THIRD REVIEW, THE ALLOW SIDE. 'without the HTML put it in Claude Docs': 'without' scopes over 'the HTML', and the un-negated verb 'put' takes Claude Docs.

artifact-style-docs-why-dont-asked._why: THIRD REVIEW, THE ALLOW SIDE. 'Why don’t we use Claude Docs' is a suggestion, like 'why not use'.

artifact-style-docs-unlisted-verb-denied._why: ALWAYS ENFORCE: A REFUSAL MUST NEVER READ AS AN ASK. don't, dont, do not and never negate whatever word comes next, listed verb or not ('don't send it to Claude Docs', 'never save it in Claude Docs'). A later listed verb does not lift that negation unless it starts a new coordinated verb ('and put it in Claude Docs'). Under the nearest-verb rule, 'Don’t send the brief you make to Claude Docs' read as an ask, because 'make' sat after the negated 'send'.

artifact-style-docs-coordinated-verb-ask._why: THE ONE WAY A STRONG NEGATION IS LIFTED. 'Don't worry about formatting and put it in Claude Docs': 'and' starts a new verb, 'put', which takes Claude Docs and is not negated. Without the coordinator exception every 'don't …' earlier in the clause would refuse the ask.

artifact-style-docs-unlisted-verb-asked._why: THE OTHER HALF OF THE VERB LIST. 'Instead of HTML share it in Claude Docs' is an ask. Exit 1 is those four unresolved kinds, which is the resolver's own error and not this assertion.

ui-direction-record-absent._why: The NEGATIVE half, and the reason the positive one cannot be asserted alone: a report that always names a record and a report that never looks are indistinguishable from a tree that happens to have one. This tree is identical except that `.claude/design/direction.md` is absent, so the flag isolates to that one file. `.claude/workforce/.keep.md` is tracked only so a `.claude/` exists — without it the resolver walks upward and reports the developer's own checkout. turn-budget-agent-hook-silent._why: MEASURED, NOT IMAGINED. The 2026-10-12 canary caught a payload nothing in the plan predicted: a `type: "agent"` hook's own agent fires PostToolUse with `agent_id: hook-agent-<uuid>` and NO `agent_type` at all. So `agent_id` alone cannot select the branch that reads a handbook -- both keys are required, or this payload sends the hook looking for `.claude/agents/None.md` on every call of every agent hook on the machine.

turn-budget-bad-stdin._why: NOT JSON AT ALL. Every hook here takes this row (`hook-badstdin`, `ledger-badstdin-is-silent`): a hook that exits nonzero or prints a traceback on a payload it cannot parse turns a harness hiccup into noise in front of the model on every call.

turn-budget-between-thresholds-quiet._why: THE SILENCE BETWEEN THE TWO INJECTIONS, AT THE TURN JUST BELOW THE SECOND. 36 of 40 is past the 80% boundary and one turn short of `maxTurns - 3`, so the warn has already been spent and the final is not yet due. Without this row the suite could not tell a correct second threshold from one that fires the moment the first has; at the adjacent turn it also catches a threshold that slipped a turn EARLY, which `turn-budget-final-returns-now` on its own cannot see.

turn-budget-eighty-percent-warns._why: 32 OF 40 IS THE 80% BOUNDARY, and this is the whole point of the hook: a cut-off that arrives unannounced delivers nothing to read back (REPORT.md 5), and an agent cannot count its own turns. The injected text must name all three artefacts the successor needs -- an OUTPUT.md with every exit criterion MET or UNMET, a HANDOFF.md continuation brief in the section shape `org.md` rung 12b verifies, and the `HANDOFF` verdict that makes rung 12b fire. IT MUST ALSO SAY WHAT RUNG 12b ACTUALLY DOES WITH THAT VERDICT: resume this same agent with `SendMessage` and a fresh turn allowance, context intact, spawning a successor only on exhausted context. Until e06d730 the rung spawned a successor and this text said so; an agent told it will be replaced writes a brief for a stranger instead of a checkpoint for itself, and `RESUME YOU` is what keeps the two from drifting apart again. `fired-warn` is the once-only marker.

turn-budget-final-returns-now._why: `maxTurns - 3` = 37 OF 40, AND THE NUMBER IS WHAT MAKES THE INSTRUCTION OBEYABLE. It was `maxTurns - 2`, and the end-to-end run of commit d782174 measured the cost of that turn: a `maxTurns: 20` IC took the final injection on turn 18, spent 19 on OUTPUT.md and 20 on HANDOFF.md, and the cap arrived before it could reply -- both files written and the HANDOFF verdict never delivered, which is the silence the hook exists to prevent. So the text asks for BOTH files in ONE turn via parallel `Write` calls and the reply on the next, and the threshold leaves three: one to write, one of slack for a retry, one to reply. The wants below pin that wording, because a text that goes back to one file per turn re-creates the measured defect at a threshold that still looks right.

turn-budget-final-marks-the-agent-handof._why: A CAP IS A CHECKPOINT, AND THE SESSION HAS TO BE TOLD WHOSE (K8). The injection is read by the AGENT; nothing in it reaches the session, so a cut run still ends with the manager holding no instruction -- the user's words, 2026-10-12: *"we're waiting on work that's never gonna get completed."* At the final threshold this hook therefore marks the agent `handoff` on its own issue in the project's ledger, through `wf-task-tag`'s own API rather than a second writer. It marks it HERE because this hook knows the `agent_id` and the count at the moment the budget runs out, where whether `SubagentStop` fires at a `maxTurns` cut is unmeasured on this host. The `handoff_digest` is the issue's UNMET set as it stands now, which is what the SECOND hand-off is compared against.

turn-budget-resumed-cap-stalls._why: THE SECOND CUT IS THE ONE THE LOOP GUARD IS FOR, and the guard is PROGRESS, never a count of resumes. This agent was already cut once (`fired-final` is claimed, its entry carries the digest of the one open item) and has been resumed: the transcript is 77 turns because the count is cumulative across a `SendMessage` resume, so the marker had to become round-keyed or the resumed run would hit its new cap in total silence -- the defect this hook exists for, one layer out. BOTH progress signals are unmoved here, which is what stalled now requires: the new digest equals the stored one, AND the three `Write` calls in the transcript are the same three the first cut recorded in `handoff_writes`, so the agent produced nothing new in the round it just spent. The entry is flagged `handoff_stalled` for the main `Stop` to escalate instead of asking for a third resume. The turn is reported WITHIN the current allowance (37 of 40, not 77 of 40), because a number past the cap reads as a bug to the agent being told it.

turn-budget-resumed-cap-with-new-writes-._why: AN AGENT THAT WROTE SOMETHING IS NOT A STALLED AGENT, and this is the row the real end-to-end run of 2026-10-13 needed and did not have. Same second cut as `turn-budget-resumed-cap-stalls` -- same cumulative 77 turns, same unmet set, same digest -- with one thing different: the transcript carries FIVE `Write` calls against the three the first cut stored, so the round produced new work. The measured defect was the opposite reading: a `maxTurns: 10` IC wrote eight files in round one and eight more in round two and was called `handoff_stalled`, because the only signal was the session's checklist and the session had written none, so both marks carried the digest of the EMPTY set. An escalation hands the issue to the USER instead of finishing it, so it is never raised on a round the agent visibly worked. `handoff_writes` is updated to 5, which is what the THIRD cut will be measured against.

turn-budget-resumed-round-is-anchored-to._why: THE TRIAL'S OWN SHAPE, AND THE DEFECT IS THAT THE RESUMED AGENT WAS TOLD NOTHING. MEASURED 2026-10-13, session `68b82f98`, cap 10: the harness cut the agent on TURN 8 of round 1, not on turn 10. The schedule it replaced multiplied the cap -- round 1's final threshold plus one cap -- so round 2's notice was booked for turn 17, the second cut came first, and the agent wrote no continuation brief at all. This transcript is that run: 8 turns, the hook's own notice arriving back as a `hook_additional_context` attachment, the resume prompt, and 7 turns more. The round is anchored to the PROMPT ROW at turn 8, so the final notice lands on turn 15 -- `round_start + cap - 3` -- and the agent is told while it still has three turns to write in. `round_start: 8` in the counter is the half that proves WHERE the anchor came from: the injection row carries text and no `tool_result`, so a reader that did not exclude the hook's own words would have anchored at turn 7 and fired at 14.

turn-budget-anchored-round-is-quiet-befo._why: THE MUTATION CHECK ON THE ROW ABOVE, one turn short of the threshold. Same cut at turn 8 and same resume, with 6 turns in the second allowance instead of 7: turn 14 is turn 6 of round 2, the notice is not due, and a hook that fired on every call after a resume -- or that re-anchored the round on the WRONG row -- announces the boundary here. The counter is the assertion that cannot be satisfied by silence: `round` 1 and `round_start` 8 say the resume was observed and the anchor recorded, so the quiet is the schedule's and not a failure to read the transcript at all.

turn-budget-exact-cut-keeps-the-whole-se._why: NOTHING REGRESSES FOR THE ROUND THAT DID END ON THE CAP. A `maxTurns: 80` producer was cut with the counter reading exactly 80, was resumed, and runs on: the anchored schedule puts its second final notice at 80 + 77 = TURN 157, which is the same turn the cap-multiple arithmetic booked, and the text reads `77 of 80` as it did before. That is the whole point of anchoring rather than re-basing: when the harness's count and ours agree, the two models agree too, and the change is only visible on the rounds that ended early. At a cap of 80 the drift is also where the measured silence costs most -- 45 cut-offs in 269 capped-IC dispatches -- so this row runs at the producer cap rather than the 10 the trial used.

turn-budget-hostile-agent-type._why: `agent_type` ARRIVES IN A PAYLOAD AND BECOMES A PATH. The value here is `../evil`, which resolves to a real `maxTurns: 40` handbook one directory above `.claude/agents/` -- so a hook that joined the name unvalidated would read it, and the same shape reaches any file on the host by lengthening the prefix. It must be refused as a name, not sanitised into one: silent, no read, no state. Same rule as `wf-org-sync`'s AGENT_SLUG_RX.

turn-budget-main-session-silent._why: THE FAST PATH THAT LICENSES RUNNING THIS ON EVERY TOOL CALL. MEASURED on Claude Code 2.1.296 (platform.md fact 22a): a PostToolUse payload from the main thread carries NO `agent_id`, and one from inside a subagent always does -- so `agent_id` is the test and `agent_type` is not, because a `--agent` main thread carries that. The tree holds a 40-turn transcript and a `maxTurns: 40` handbook, so every threshold is passed; the only reason nothing fires is the identity branch. `after` asserts NO state directory was created, which is the half that proves no file I/O happened at all.

turn-budget-malformed-state-recovers._why: THE STATE FILE IS SCRATCH IN A WORLD-WRITABLE DIRECTORY, so it can hold anything. A hook that raised on it would print a traceback into the transcript of every tool call for the rest of the run. Unparsable state is discarded and the count re-derived from the transcript, which is the whole reason the transcript is the source of truth and the file is only a cache.

turn-budget-no-maxturns-silent._why: A LEAD HAS NO CAP, SO IT GETS NO BOUNDARY. `handbook-templates.md` gives `maxTurns` to the IC template and to no other tier, so a handbook without the key is the ordinary shape of every Lead and CEO on every host. The boundary is derived from the cap and from nothing else: with no cap there is no 80% of anything, and a hook that guessed one would stop an uncapped employee at a number no file states.

turn-budget-under-threshold-silent._why: 31 TURNS OF 40 IS BELOW 80%, so the boundary must not fire. The row is the negative half of the pair below and the whole reason the count is of TURNS rather than calls: measured in REPORT.md 2, report orders ran 42 and 44 CALLS inside a 40-turn cap and both finished, so a per-call boundary would have stopped two runs that were fine. State IS written here -- the offset and running count are what keep the next call cheap.

turn-budget-unknown-agent-silent._why: WIRED AT USER SCOPE, RUNNING IN EVERY PROJECT ON THE MACHINE -- most of which have no org at all. An `agent_type` with no handbook under `.claude/agents/` has no cap to read, so there is no boundary to announce and nothing may be invented from a default. Silent, and no state written.

turn-budget-unreadable-transcript-counts._why: NO TRANSCRIPT ON DISK, SO IT COUNTS CALLS, WHICH ERRS TOWARD AN EARLY HANDOFF. There is no transcript file in this tree at all. Calls >= turns always, so a call count crosses the boundary no later than the true turn count -- the conservative direction, because an early written hand-back costs one order and a silent cut-off costs the whole run. The stored count is 7, this call makes 8, and 8 is past both boundaries of a cap of 10. UNDER `maxTurns - 3` A SMALL CAP TAKES THE FINAL TEXT, NOT THE 80% ONE: 10 puts the final at 7 and the warn at 8, so the final is due first and the stronger one speaks, spending the warn unspoken. That is why the wants name only what both texts carry. It costs the run nothing, because the final text carries the whole instruction -- both files, their seven sections, and the verdict.

turn-budget-warn-fires-once._why: ONE INSTRUCTION, ONCE. PostToolUse fires on every tool call, so a boundary that re-announced itself would repeat the same paragraph eight times between 32 and 40 and teach its reader it is noise -- the failure that retired the speech guards (changes/1.30.1.md). The marker is a separate `O_EXCL` file rather than a flag inside the counter, because parallel tool calls in one turn fire this hook concurrently and a read-modify-write of one JSON file can lose the flag and inject twice.

turn-budget-counter-symlink-not-followed._why: THE SAME ATTACK ONE LEVEL IN: the directories are ours, and a symlink is planted at `count.json` aiming at a file outside them. Both halves of the refusal are asserted here. The READ is `O_NOFOLLOW`, so the link is refused rather than followed -- without it this is an arbitrary-file read aimed by whoever planted the link.
